This Memorandum of Appeal is preferred by the appellant under Section 29 of PWDV Act challenging the order passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Traffic Court-V, Bengaluru in Crl.Misc.No.364/2011, dated:18.07.2018 as to dismissing the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 12 of PWDV Act.
2. The appellants herein were the petitioners and the respondents herein was the respondents before the trial Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 court.
For the sake of convenience, parties would be referred to by the ranks they were assigned before the trial court.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.1 was solemnized on 4.02.2004 at Sri Vasavi Kannika Parameshwari Prathana Kalyana Mantapa as per Hindu customs and rites.

4. In the grounds, the appellant/petitioner No.1 has contended that the trial court has erred in dismissing the petition and it is illegal, invalid, improper and not in accordance with law and hence,
liable to be set aside.
The trial court has placed much reliance on the unacceptable contention of the respondents, which are inadmissible.
The contention taken before the trial court by the respondents is manifestly erroneous and the trial court ought not to have dismissed the petition.
The trial court has grossly erred in law and not appreciated that the respondent No.1 has harassed and tortured the appellant No.1 and failed to pay the maintenance.
There is severe threat to the appellant and the said fact has been overlooked by the trial court.

The trial court has failed to observe that the appellant No.1 was residing in the portion of the house and the respondents during her stay, used to harass and torture her and thrown her out of the house and when the panchayat was convened, the appellant was been provided Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 with shelter and subsequently continued to harass her.
The respondent No.1 has suppressed the material facts before the trial court just to escape from providing shelter and to pay the maintenance and compensation.

The respondent No.1 has filed a petition for restitution of conjugal right before the Family Court and the same was allowed.
In spite of it, the respondent No.1 did not maintain the appellant and continued to harass and torture her.
Hence, the petition is filed and the trial court without considering the reliefs under Section 12 of PWDV Act, has dismissed the petition.
There was an interim order of granting maintenance of Rs.3,000/- per month, but while passing the order on merit, the petition itself is dismissed.
The appellant/petitioner is facing financial crises and starvation.

The appellant is an Unemployee and Uneducated woman and she has to maintain her children i.e., appellant Nos.2 & 3 and has to take care care of the education of the children, who are pursuing studies in Holy Child Convent and Holy Kids School.

Accordingly, the domestic relationship between the parties as defined under Section 2(f)of PWDV Act is taken as proved.
10. It is also observed to grant the relief under Section 2(f) of PWDV Act, the petitioner No.1 has to prove the domestic violence by the respondent No.1 and she is the aggrieved person.

It is the main allegation considered by the trial court that the petitioner No.1 in her affidavit in view of her examination in chief, has alleged that the respondent Nos.2 to 4 used to instigate the respondent No.1 to assault her and the said allegation is vague.
No specific incident is mentioned with respect to the said allegation.
She has not produced the corroborative evidence to prove the same.
The cross examination of P.W.1 s relied by the trial court and according to it, there is admission that they are residing in III Floor and the In-laws are residing in Ground Floor.

Under such circumstances,
Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 the trial court has relied upon the dictum of the Hon'ble High Court of Rajasthan in Crl. Mis. (Pet.) No.1524/2011 (Sudama Dutt Sharma .Vs. State of Rajasthan) , wherein Their Lordships have clearly held that, "in the absence of concrete proof relating to the instance of domestic violence, a casual reference of name of family members without their being any allegation of their active involvement in the matter is sufficient to conclude that the complaint is in-fact designed to harass the respondents" .
Hence, the trial court has come to the conclusion that the petitioner No.1 is not entitle to claim any relief against the respondent Nos.2 to 4.
Therefore, the trial court is justified to that extent as per the observations.

The concept and proposition of Section 13 in The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 is to be considered, which reads thus :
 Welfare of minor to be paramount  consideration.--
( 1) In the appointment or declaration of any person as guardian of a Hindu minor by a court, the welfare of the minor shall be the paramount consideration.

Therefore, the evidence and its appreciation and reasonings assigned by the trial court as to voluntarily withdrawing from the company of respondent by the petitioner by itself does not absolve the liability of the husband/respondent to maintain his wife and children.

In the decision reported in 1991(2) SCC 375 (K.Vimala .Vs. Veeraswamy ), Their Lordships have clearly observed as under:
Section 125 of the code of Criminal Procedure is meant to achieve a social purpose.
The object is to prevent vagrancy and destitution.
It provides a speedy remedy for the supply of food, clothing and shelter to the deserted wife.

The woman not having the legal status of a wife is thus brought within the inclusive definition of the term "Wife"
consistent with the objective.
Thus, man who lived with woman for a long time made liable to pay maintenance.
The man should not be allowed enjoy advantage of a de-facto marriage without undertaking the duties and obligations.

Any other interpretation would lead the woman to "vagrancy and destitution"

In another decision reported in (2014) ACR 436 (Shamim Bano .Vs. Asraf Khan) , Their Lordships have clearly observed as under:
"Another aspect which has to be kept uppermost in mind is that when the marriage breaks up, a woman suffers from emotional fractures, fragmentation Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 of sentiments, loss of economic and social security and in certain cases, inadequate requisites for survival.
A marriage is fundamentally a unique bond between two parties.
When it perishes like a mushroom, the dignity of the female fame gets corroded.
It is the law's duty to recompense and primary obligation is that of a husband.
Needless to emphasize the entitlement and necessitous provisions have to be made in accordance with the parameters of law".

21. In another decision reported in 1982 Criminal Law Journal 485 (Basanta Kumari Mohanty .Vs.
Sarat Kumar Mohanty) , Their Lordshis have clearly observed as under:
"The object of the provisions being to prevent vagrancy and destitution, it has to be found out as to what is required by the wife to maintain a standard of living which is neither luxurious nor penurious; but is modestly consistent with the status of the family.

The trial court has to consider the comprehensive totality of evidence intended to be adduced by the appellant Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 as well as further evidence, if any on behalf of the respondent and to pass justifiable order.
The detailed discussion and appreciation of evidence is essential so as to correlate with the facts and circumstances of the case.
The trial court has to look into the aspect of interse denial or refusal or withdrawal from the society of the spouse each other will not affect the family members, more particularly the child.
The desertion or otherwise and the domestic violence and harassment, cruelty are supposed to be considered in this petition.
The dispute between the parents should not deprive the children from growing in congenial atmosphere in the society to brought up in a respectable manner as respectable citizen of India.
The child shall not be made destitute or orphan due to irretrievable and irreconcilable relationship between the spouse.
They should not suffer due to lack of love and affection of the parents.
They have to be mentally and physically healthy and have need association of the parents, who are looking after their paramount interest.
23. The welfare and paramount interest of the child is to be looked into while passing the order in consonance with purport and object of the statute.
The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 and The Guardian & Wards Act provides for protection to the minor so as to lead the life under the guardianship of parents.

The provisions of Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 PWDV Act also provides for awarding maintenance in correlation with the other beneficial provision enure to the benefit of wife Smt.M.Jyothi vs Sri.M.Saravana on 2 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120447495/

and children.

Therefore, the petition is deserves to be allowed in part.

The matrimonial relationship between herself and respondent No.1 was completely broken.
There is no safety to the life of petitioners in th hands of the respondent No.1.
Hence, from May 2011, she is residing at her parents house along with her children.
She has no source of income.
Hence, the petitioner No.1 has filed the petition under Section 12 of PWDV Act.
After due process and procedure, the trial court has dismissed the petition filed by the petitioners.
The contention taken before the trial court by the respondents is manifestly erroneous and the trial court ought not to have dismissed the petition.
The trial court has grossly erred in law and not appreciated that the respondent No.1 has harassed and tortured the appellant No.1 and failed to pay the maintenance.
There is severe threat to the appellant and the said fact has been overlooked by the trial court.
The trial court has failed to observe that the appellant No.1 was residing in the portion of the house and the respondents during her stay, used to harass and torture her and thrown her out of the house and when the panchayat was convened, the appellant was been provided Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 with shelter and subsequently continued to harass her.
The respondent No.1 has suppressed the material facts before the trial court just to escape from providing shelter and to pay the maintenance and compensation.
The appellant has proved prima-facie case against the respondent No.1 and the trial court has not considered the same and dismissed the petition.
The respondent No.1 has filed a petition for restitution of conjugal right before the Family Court and the same was allowed.
In spite of it, the respondent No.1 did not maintain the appellant and continued to harass and torture her.
Hence, the petition is filed and the trial court without considering the reliefs under Section 12 of PWDV Act, has dismissed the petition.

4. In the grounds, the appellant/petitioner No.1 has contended that the trial court has erred in dismissing the petition and it is illegal, invalid, improper and not in accordance with law and hence,
liable to be set aside.
The trial court has placed much reliance on the unacceptable contention of the respondents, which are inadmissible.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. After hearing the arguments, the points raised for determination are as under:
1.
Whether the appellants have made out grounds to intermeddle with the impugned order ?
2. What Order ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The trial court has to consider the comprehensive totality of evidence intended to be adduced by the appellant Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 as well as further evidence, if any on behalf of the respondent and to pass justifiable order.
The detailed discussion and appreciation of evidence is essential so as to correlate with the facts and circumstances of the case.
The trial court has to look into the aspect of interse denial or refusal or withdrawal from the society of the spouse each other will not affect the family members, more particularly the child.
The desertion or otherwise and the domestic violence and harassment, cruelty are supposed to be considered in this petition.
The dispute between the parents should not deprive the children from growing in congenial atmosphere in the society to brought up in a respectable manner as respectable citizen of India.
The child shall not be made destitute or orphan due to irretrievable and irreconcilable relationship between the spouse.
They should not suffer due to lack of love and affection of the parents.
They have to be mentally and physically healthy and have need association of the parents, who are looking after their paramount interest.
23. The welfare and paramount interest of the child is to be looked into while passing the order in consonance with purport and object of the statute.
The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 and The Guardian & Wards Act provides for protection to the minor so as to lead the life under the guardianship of parents.
Therefore, the respondent being the father, has to maintain the children.
The obligation is incidental to the marriage and birth of the children and it cannot be stated that the mother only capable and responsible to maintain the children.

24. POINT No.2 : My finding on this point is as per following :
O R DE R The Crl.
Appeal filed by the appellant is hereby allowed in part.
Consequently, the impugned order passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate,
Traffic Court-V, Bengaluru in Crl.Misc.No.364/2011, dated:18.07.2018 is set aside.
The respondent No.1 is directed to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/- each per month to the appellant/petitioner Nos.2 and 3 as and when the same fell due from time to time from the date of impugned order till the petitioner No.2 attains majority and got married and till the petitioner No.3 attains majority.
Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018
Further, the respondent No.1 shall also pay a sum of Rs.50,000/- each per annum to the appellant/petitioner Nos.2 and 3 for their educational as well as medical expenses.
So far as the petitioner No.1 is concerned, the order of trial court is confirmed.
Sent back the records to the trial court along with the copy of this judgment.
